topics.title: The sun, the moon and the stars

learn.hook: Look up! By day the sun shines, and at night the moon and thousands of stars twinkle.
points: The sun is a star. It is the star nearest to the Earth, and it gives us light and heat.
The sun looks small only because it is very far away. It is much, much bigger than the Earth.
The moon goes around the Earth. It has no light of its own. It shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces back to us.

Stars are huge, hot balls of glowing gas. They look tiny because they are very, very far away. Groups of stars that make patterns are called constellations. The Saptarishi is a famous pattern of seven bright stars.
Never look straight at the sun, not even with sunglasses. It can badly hurt your eyes.

example.q: Think it through: Stars are in the sky during the day too. Why can't we see them?
steps: The stars are still there in the daytime.
The sun is so close and bright that its light fills the sky.
The faint starlight is hidden by the bright sunlight.
example.answer: The bright sunlight hides the much fainter light of the stars.

learn.reallife: On a clear night, away from city lights, look for the seven bright stars of the Saptarishi. With an adult, see if you can spot the Pole Star.

Stars look tiny because they are very far away.

quiz.q: What is the sun?
quiz.explain: The sun is a star, a huge ball of hot, glowing gas.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun is a planet

quiz.q: Why does the moon shine?
options: Sunlight falls on it and bounces back
quiz.explain: The moon has no light of its own. It reflects the light of the sun.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the moon makes its own light

quiz.q: Why does the sun look small in the sky?
options: Because it is a tiny star
Because it is smaller than a football
Because it is very far away
quiz.explain: The sun is far bigger than the Earth. It only looks small because it is so far away.
quiz.mistake: Thinks things are as small as they look

quiz.q: The Pole Star helps travellers find which direction?
quiz.explain: The Pole Star (Dhruv Tara) stays above the North, so it shows the North direction.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the direction shown by the Pole Star

quiz.q: How many bright stars make the Saptarishi pattern?
quiz.explain: 'Sapta' means seven. The Saptarishi is a pattern of seven bright stars.
quiz.mistake: Does not link 'sapta' with seven

quiz.q: On which date in 2023 did India's Chandrayaan-3 land on the moon?
quiz.explain: Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram landed near the moon's south pole on 23 August 2023. India celebrates this day as National Space Day.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the landing date with national holidays

quiz.q: Why must we never look straight at the sun?
options: It will make the sun angry
It can badly hurt our eyes
quiz.explain: The sun's light is so strong that it can damage our eyes, even with sunglasses.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the danger of looking at the sun

quiz.q: What goes around the Earth?
quiz.explain: The moon goes around the Earth. The Earth goes around the sun.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun goes around the Earth

teach.ask: Gappu thinks the moon is a lamp in the sky. Can you tell him about the sun, the moon and the stars?
teach.praise: Superstar! The sun is a star, the moon shines with the sun's light, and stars look tiny because they are far away.
teach.nudge: Does the moon make its own light, or does it get light from somewhere?

learn.hook: The sun seems to rise and set, but it is actually the Earth that is spinning!
points: The Earth is shaped like a ball (a sphere). It spins around itself all the time, like a top.
The side of the Earth facing the sun has day. The side facing away from the sun has night.
One full spin takes about 24 hours. That gives us one day and one night.
Because the Earth spins from west to east, the sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.
The Earth also goes around the sun. One full trip takes about 365 days, which is one year.

example.q: Think it through: Your cousin lives in America. When you are going to school in the morning in India, she is getting ready for bed. Why?
steps: The Earth is a ball that spins.
Only half of it faces the sun at a time.
India and America are on different sides of the Earth.
When India faces the sun, much of America faces away from it.
example.answer: Because when India has day, America is on the side of the Earth facing away from the sun, so it has night.

learn.reallife: In a dark room, with an adult, shine a torch on a ball and turn it slowly. Watch day and night move around the ball!

items.text: The Earth spins around itself once in about ___ hours.
The side of the Earth facing the sun has ___.
The Earth goes around the sun in about ___ days.
The sun seems to rise in the ___.

quiz.q: What causes day and night?
options: The sun going around the Earth
quiz.explain: As the Earth spins, each place turns towards the sun (day) and then away from it (night).
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun moves around the Earth

quiz.q: About how many hours does the Earth take to spin around once?
quiz.explain: One full spin of the Earth takes about 24 hours, which is one day and one night.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the time for one spin with the time for one trip around the sun

quiz.q: About how many days does the Earth take to go once around the sun?
quiz.explain: The Earth takes about 365 days to go around the sun. That is one year.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Earth's spin with its trip around the sun

quiz.q: What is the shape of the Earth?
quiz.explain: The Earth is round like a ball. That is why only half of it gets sunlight at a time.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Earth is flat

quiz.q: In which direction does the sun seem to rise?
quiz.explain: The Earth spins from west to east, so the sun seems to come up in the east.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the directions of sunrise and sunset

quiz.q: If it is daytime in India, what is it on the side of the Earth facing away from the sun?
quiz.explain: The side facing away from the sun gets no sunlight, so it has night.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is day everywhere at the same time

quiz.q: A torch is shone on a spinning ball in a dark room. What does the torch stand for?
quiz.explain: The torch gives light like the sun, and the ball is like the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the light source with the Earth

quiz.q: How many hours are there in 3 full days?
quiz.explain: Each day has 24 hours. 24 × 3 = 72 hours.
quiz.mistake: Adds 24 and 3 or multiplies wrongly

teach.ask: Gappu thinks the sun goes to sleep at night. What really causes day and night?
teach.praise: Bravo! The Earth spins, and the side facing the sun has day while the other side has night.
teach.nudge: Does the sun move around the Earth, or does the Earth do something?

learn.hook: Some nights the moon is a thin smile, some nights a full round plate. Is it really changing shape?
points: The moon does not really change its shape. Half of it is always lit by the sun.
As the moon goes around the Earth, we see different amounts of its lit part. These changing shapes are called phases of the moon.
On the new moon night (Amavasya), we cannot see the moon. On the full moon night (Purnima), we see a full round moon.
After the new moon, the lit part grows night by night: crescent, half moon, then full moon. After the full moon, it shrinks again.
From one full moon to the next takes about 29 and a half days, nearly a month.

example.q: Think it through: Tonight is a full moon. About how many days until the next full moon?
steps: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to go through all its phases.
So the next full moon comes after about 29 or 30 days.
example.answer: About 29 to 30 days, nearly a month.

learn.reallife: Keep a moon diary for a month. Each night, draw the moon's shape and watch it grow and shrink.

games.title: Moon phase facts
items: The moon really changes its shape every night.
The moon stays round. We just see different amounts of its lit part.
On a new moon night, we cannot see the moon.
The lit side faces away from us, so the moon is not visible.
From one full moon to the next takes about 29 and a half days.
That is why we see about one full moon each month.
After the full moon, the lit part we see gets smaller each night.
The moon wanes, or shrinks, until the next new moon.
Purnima is the full moon night.
On Purnima, the whole lit face of the moon is towards us.

quiz.q: What are the phases of the moon?
options: The different shapes of the moon we see during a month
quiz.explain: Phases are the changing shapes of the moon's lit part that we see from the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the moon actually breaks or changes

quiz.q: On which night can we NOT see the moon?
quiz.explain: On the new moon night, the lit side of the moon faces away from the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up new moon and full moon

quiz.q: About how many days pass from one full moon to the next?
quiz.explain: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to go through all its phases.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the moon's cycle with a week or a year

quiz.q: Does the moon really change its shape?
options: No, we only see different amounts of its lit part
quiz.explain: The moon is always round. Its lit part faces us by different amounts.
quiz.mistake: Believes the moon's shape really changes

quiz.q: Diwali is celebrated on a new moon night. What will the sky look like on Diwali night?
quiz.explain: On a new moon night, the moon is not seen. The lamps make Diwali night bright!
quiz.mistake: Does not link new moon with a moonless sky

quiz.q: Which shape comes after the new moon as the moon starts to grow?
quiz.explain: After the new moon, a thin curved crescent appears first, then it grows.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of the phases

quiz.q: Why is half of the moon always lit?
options: The sun always shines on the half facing it
quiz.explain: Like the Earth, the moon has a sunny side. The half facing the sun is always lit.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the moon makes light

quiz.q: A full moon is seen on day 0. On about which day will the next full moon come?
quiz.explain: The full cycle takes about 29 and a half days, so the next full moon comes on day 29 or 30.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a full moon comes every week or every 15 days

teach.ask: Gappu saw a round moon last week and a thin moon tonight. Did the moon break? Please explain!
teach.praise: Magical! The moon is always round. We just see different amounts of its sunlit part. These are its phases!
teach.nudge: Is the moon really changing, or are we seeing a different amount of its lit part?
